hypothesis.title: Voice analysis for mental health assessment
hypothesis.population: Adults (≥18 years) with or without mental health conditions
hypothesis.intervention: Acoustic feature extraction and machine‑learning analysis of speech recordings
hypothesis.outcome: Accurate detection or quantification of mental health status (e.g., depression, anxiety) compared with standard clinical assessments
hypothesis.clinical_context: Screening and monitoring of mental health in primary care or tele‑health settings
hypothesis.relationship_type: Predictive association (voice features predict mental health status)

plan.study_goal: Voice analysis for mental health assessment

steps.name: Literature Review & Feasibility Assessment
steps.description: Conduct a systematic review of existing voice‑based mental‑health biomarkers and evaluate technical, ethical, and logistical feasibility of implementing acoustic analysis in a primary‑care/tele‑health setting.

steps.name: Study Protocol Development
steps.description: Draft a detailed protocol outlining objectives, inclusion/exclusion criteria (≥18 years, with and without diagnosed depression/anxiety), sample size calculation, study design (cross‑sectional diagnostic accuracy), data collection procedures, and statistical analysis plan.

steps.name: Ethics & Regulatory Approvals
steps.description: Submit the protocol, informed‑consent forms, and data‑privacy safeguards to an Institutional Review Board (IRB) and, if required, to data‑protection authorities; obtain all necessary approvals before recruitment.

steps.name: Participant Recruitment & Screening
steps.description: Recruit a representative adult cohort (e.g., 300 participants) from primary‑care clinics and tele‑health platforms. Screen for eligibility, obtain informed consent, and record demographic/clinical baseline data.

steps.name: Standard Clinical Assessment
steps.description: Administer validated mental‑health instruments (e.g., PHQ‑9 for depression, GAD‑7 for anxiety) and, when applicable, structured clinical interviews (SCID) to establish reference diagnoses.

steps.name: Speech Data Collection
steps.description: Capture high‑quality audio recordings in a standardized setting (e.g., 5‑minute read passage, spontaneous interview, and picture‑description tasks) using calibrated microphones or secure mobile apps.

steps.name: Acoustic Feature Extraction
steps.description: Process recordings with open‑source toolkits (e.g., OpenSMILE, Praat) to extract low‑level descriptors (pitch, jitter, shimmer, formants, MFCCs) and higher‑order statistical features; store features in a secure database.

steps.name: Machine‑Learning Model Development
steps.description: Split the dataset into training (70 %) and hold‑out test (30 %) sets. Train multiple algorithms (e.g., logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting, deep neural nets) using cross‑validation, and select the best model based on AUC‑ROC, sensitivity, and specificity.

steps.name: Statistical Validation & Comparative Analysis
steps.description: Evaluate model performance against the clinical reference standard, calculate diagnostic accuracy metrics, conduct subgroup analyses (age, gender, comorbidities), and assess calibration and decision‑curve analysis for clinical utility.

steps.name: Reporting, Dissemination & Implementation Planning
steps.description: Prepare a manuscript following STARD‑AI and CONSORT‑AI guidelines, present findings at conferences, and develop a roadmap for integrating the validated voice‑based tool into primary‑care workflows (e.g., API for tele‑health platforms).
